reviews.scope_depth_novelty: A coherent and substantive comparison of timestamp clock-source, unit, wrap, reuse and age hypotheses with a bounded discriminator. Its source-comparator versus installed-provider boundary and unchanged full-triple gate are well handled. The incorrect aged count reverses the report's rare-event framing, so Main must use the correction below rather than its current executive summary.

corrections.claim_in_report: The 20-second aged run had 140/141 valid full triples and one start-before-submit failure.
corrections.pinned_receipt: event-service-clock-age-aged-v2.json records invalid_timestamps=140, timestamp_qualified=false; its 141 samples contain 140 submit_order=0 and one submit_order=1.
corrections.corrected_fact: The aged run had 140/141 start-before-submit failures and 1/141 full-triple pass. All 141 end-start deltas pass the receipt's positive-service and 52 ns granularity predicates; observed minimum delta is 937 ns.
corrections.impact: This is a widespread ordering failure in this one aged cohort, not a rare isolated event. It strengthens the association with the 20-second wait in this paired run but does not establish wait causality, NTP/system-clock cause, or a general production-profile failure rate. Preserve the failed aged status and full-triple acceptance unchanged.

corrections.claim_in_report: The model receipt is described as a 32,768-token prefill run.
corrections.pinned_receipt: The bench option requests a 32,768-token minimum, while benchmark_result.results.prompts['32768-minimum'] reports actual_prompt_tokens=39262 and actual_read_tokens=39262; the engine placement line reports tokens=39261, context=65536, chunk=8192.
corrections.corrected_fact: Describe this as a 32,768-token minimum-request run with an actual 39,262-token prompt (39,261 engine placement rows), at 65,536 context and 8,192 chunking.

corrections.claim_in_report: The receipt discussion can be read as if the model diagnostic itself pins every loaded runtime/driver ELF.
corrections.pinned_receipt: The event-service baseline/aged receipts contain runtime-ready executed_ELF_sha256 maps for SYCL, UR adapter/loader, Level Zero loader/driver, IGC and compiler ELF. The model diagnostic pins its engine binary and environment/adapter path but does not carry that loaded-ELF map.
corrections.corrected_fact: Attribute loaded ELF hashes to the separate clock-age microtests; do not claim they are independently proven for the model diagnostic process. The model capture still records the selected UR adapter path and exact engine binary.

reviews.corrected_operational_read: Model profile: 508 accepted records plus 24 rejected records among 532 captured numeric events; all 24 rejects are start<submit. Baseline clock microtest passes 141/141; its 20-second aged arm fails start<submit for 140/141 while all 141 durations remain positive and above the recorded 52 ns granularity. The wait relationship is a diagnostic association only; exact installed UR source mapping, raw clock cause and performance conclusions remain absent.
reviews.source_quality_provenance: Uses Khronos SYCL 2020 R12 and versioned Level Zero 1.19.12 documents plus immutable Intel LLVM snapshot afcca05be916a6ba0b925a4e088d76c160442be2 as a comparator. The report correctly refuses to infer installed source identity from clang 22.1 or an upstream v2 snapshot. The cited Intel source has Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception; no prohibited implementation source was used.

reviews.scope_depth_novelty: Strong source-level audit of the exact custom native16/TLA adapter and its route-map producer, job scalars, queue sequencing, checked host readback, ownership and combine contract. It corrects the earlier R994 generic oneMKL attribution and makes the all-GPU residual versus host route-map tail distinction explicit. It is distinct from R993 expert-weight staging and R995's previously eligible question; no route performance conclusion is supported.
reviews.source_quality_provenance: Four source hashes were rechecked against the assigned worktree and command-service build-v2 source_pins; the build receipt records source_commit af99f2943b2c782d6691d5500ea852e2169dd02f. The report correctly says Git identity/ancestry was not verified. Target source is repository MIT; the public SYCL specification is a semantics reference only. No XeStrata implementation code/design was consulted or adopted.
reviews.scope_limit: The report is a completed source-contract investigation, not a measured CPU bottleneck, dispatch proposal, speed estimate, quality result or adoption decision. The prior R997 profile gaps remain open.

reviews.scope_depth_novelty: Substantive within budget. It distinguishes gathered expert A and SwiGLU A2 operand lifetimes, scale and rounding boundaries, target consumer tuple limits, quantization costs, and a concrete BF16 fused SwiGLU-to-down-GEMM alternative. There is moderate overlap with R989 on Xe2 INT8 matrix availability and R993 on MoE expert staging; the new activation-only constraint (current FP16/BF16 weight operand does not form the documented INT8 pair) and fusion alternative give it a distinct retrieval value.
reviews.source_quality_provenance: Uses pinned vLLM commit 2b85d9cb65c1f56c347cb7f56f1596a6b8b28373 and SGLang commit eb5739b30e7e5cb2d7833a8952a24e4e470718f8 as backend-specific numerical/design examples; Intel SYCL matrix-extension commit 4a08d0453c6b37a6e1eb5f52933f79c734b1149c and versioned VTune docs for advertised formats; OCP MX v1.0 for scale format. The oneAPI tuple is optional and not an installed-device/runtime proof; no speed, quality or support result is claimed. No code was copied and XeStrata remains excluded.
